le_buffer_finalize.role: LUT / LAB-cell OUTPUT buffer -> the SOURCE of the LUT-output routing hop (feeds C4/R4/R24/C16/LI arcs).
le_buffer_finalize.mis_classification_fixed: The pdb allocator-sim (RouteFanoutDdb._simulate_allocator, node_slot=(array_index+2512)%44260) is only valid for array_index in [20044,41747]. ALL 20640 LE_BUFFER nodes have array_index in [17,11267] -- ENTIRELY below that window -- so their rotated slot lands in the on-disk EMPTY region and the sim REFUSES all of them (0 grounded). If the linear rotation were extended (bluffed) past its window, LE_BUFFER back-ref sources would rotate onto OTHER nodes' templates -- predominantly C4/R4/R24/C16 metal -- mis-tagging the LUT-output source as metal. The enum codec labels these 20640 nodes LE_BUFFER authoritatively and design-independently, so classification no longer depends on the broken rotation: the metal mis-tag is eliminated by construction (decode-or-refuse).
le_buffer_finalize.binding_path: With the source correctly typed LE_BUFFER, the LUT-output hop binds via the device-file route resolver DYGR_DIE_INFO_BODY::get_fanout @0x127e90 + DYGR_ROUTE_ASM_INFO::get_bits_from_source_to_dest @0x228d60 (NOT the allocator sim). Proven where fanout is grounded: the 2 trace LE_BUFFER-source arcs reproduce bit-exact (8 selector bits each). Device-wide realization of all 20640 is the T2 edge sweep (sweep_le_fanout.py) -- a distinct target; this codec is its enabling classifier.
